name: The Class for Representing a Bank Account (Case 2)
description: Construct a class that represents a basic bank account. This class should contain data representing the name of the account’s owner, the account number, and the account’s current balance; all of which could be accessed or changed only through the getter and setter methods. An instance of the class should be created by specifying three parameters that are used to initialize the instance (i.e., object) data. The other methods of this class should:\n - provide a one-line description of the account, and\n - perform various services on the account (making deposits, withdrawals, adding interest to the account). These methods should examine the data passed into them to make sure the requested transaction is valid.

comments.content: We define the class Account2 to represent a bank account with basic services as well as a service to provide the account description.

To specify the initial state of a bank account, we need to have an __init__ method in the class Account2 that accepts initial values for the bank account. The __init__ accepts the name of the bank account, account number, and initial balance and stores them into the new Account2 object’s acct_name, acct_number, and balance, respectively.

The __init__ method is run automatically by Python each time an instance is created. The argument (named self) is passed in automatically by the interpreter when the method is invoked on an instance of the class.

Note that Python automatically fills the first argument in with the instance object that is the implied subject of the method call. Therefore, when this method is invoked on an instance of the class, the last three parameters must be passed to the method.

This statement sets the instance attribute acct_name to the first parameter value (owner).
self is the instance of the class and self.__acct_name is the account name. We start the attribute name by two underscore (self.__acct_name) to prevent accessing the attribute directly from outside of the class.

This statement sets instance attribute acct_number to the second parameter value (account).
self is the instance of the class and self.__acct_number is the account number. We start the attribute name by two underscore (self.__acct_number) to prevent accessing the attribute directly from outside of the class.

This statement sets instance attribute balance to the third parameter value (initial).
self is the instance of the class and self.__balance is the account's balance. We start the attribute name by two underscore (self.__balance) to prevent accessing the attribute directly from outside of the class.
This method returns a one-line description of the account as a string. The argument (named self) is passed in automatically by the interpreter when the method is invoked on an instance of the class.
Note that this method is called automatically when we pass an Account2's object to a print method (or when we concatenate an Account2's object to a string).

This statement returns the account attributes. We call format function to format the string so that all values are right-aligned with sufficient spacing between values.
{:d} is replaced by the account number
{:>20s} right-justifies the account's name in a field that is 20-characters wide
{:>10.2f} right-justifies the balance with two decimal digits in a field that is 10-characters wide.

The format function returns the result of replacing each {…} placeholder in the template string with its corresponding argument passed to the format function. Anything else, which is not contained in curly braces will be literally printed, i.e. without any changes.

Also, the format specification inside a pair of curly braces starts with a : and followed by the text that specifies the data type. The data type d requires a decimal argument, the data type s requires a string argument, and the data type f requires a floating-point argument. An error will occur if the argument is not the expected data type.

This method deposits the specified amount into this account and returns the new balance. The balance is not modified if the deposit amount is invalid. Note that the first argument (named self) is passed in automatically by the interpreter when the method is invoked on an instance of the class.

Python automatically fills the first argument in with the instance object that is the implied subject of the method call. Therefore, when this method is invoked on an instance of the class, only the last parameter (amount) must be passed to the method.
Before we add the specified amount to the balance, we need to perform a test to check whether the deposit amount is valid.

The if statement tests whether the deposit amount is greater than 0. If the deposit amount is greater than 0, then the body of this if statement gets executed. Otherwise, the body of this if statement is skipped.

This method withdraws the specified amount and fee from this account and returns the new balance. The balance is not modified if either the withdraw amount or fee are invalid or the balance is insufficient. Note that the first argument (named self) is passed in automatically by the interpreter when the method is invoked on an instance of the class.

Python automatically fills the first argument in with the instance object that is the implied subject of the method call. Therefore, when this method is invoked on an instance of the class, only the last two parameters must be passed to the method.
Before we withdraw the specified amount and fee from the account, we need to perform a test to check whether the withdraw amount and fee are valid and the balance is sufficient.

The if statement tests whether the withdraw amount is greater than zero, fee is greater than or equal to zero, and the balance is sufficient. If the withdraw amount and fee are valid and the balance is sufficient, then the body of this if statement gets executed. Otherwise, the body of this if statement is skipped.
